newsitem.title: USA: New Mexico 'escape tunnel' called a hoax by guards.
newsitem.headline: New Mexico 'escape tunnel' called a hoax by guards.

text.p: Claims by New Mexico's governor that prison inmates had dug a tunnel and were planning a riot to cover an escape bid were dismissed on Friday as a political hoax by the state prison guards' union.

A 30-foot (9 metre) tunnel at the state penitentiary said by Gov. Gary Johnson's office to have been dug by prisoners, was really a service tunnel shown in the prison blueprints, according to the Department of Public Safety.

The state corrections department said on Friday they were extending a 3-day-old lockdown at the state penitentiary near Santa Fe where they said they had uncovered a violent escape plan on Wednesday. They claimed prisoners had been extending the tunnel.
But as state legislators approved a bill on Friday to grant $3 million toward transferring some 256 prisoners to a facility in Arizona, a guards' union official branded the claims a deception.
"It's just a hoax to put pressure on the legislature and make it do the governor's bidding," said John La Bonard, a spokesman for the state prison guards' union.

Department of Public Safety Secretary Darren White said on Friday the tunnel was a "crawl space", and that a kitchen reported to have been built by prisoners inside the tunnel was a place for prison officers to heat up their lunch.
"There is no evidence that indicates that any inmates used that prison crawl space," said White.

The announcement of an escape tunnel and imposition of a state of emergency at the prison raised questions by the prison guards' union as to whether it was staged to help Johnson pass his ambitious prison building plan through the state legislature.

Johnson, a Republican, has been pushing to build more prisons for over two years. Less than 30 days remain of New Mexico's legislative session for him to gain funding for new, private prisons to house around 2,400 inmates.

Asked by reporters on Friday whether the discovery of the escape tunnel and kitchen was a hoax, Johnson sidestepped giving a direct reply, saying only that the dangers of prisoner insurrection were very real.
"Imagine if there had been a riot and there had been deaths and I had done nothing," he said on local television.
Johnson said his call for a state of emergency at the prison had likely held off a riot and given corrections officials time to transfer inmates to a private facility in Arizona.
Legislators have already approved $500,000 worth of funding for the first month of the prisoners' stay in Arizona.
Johnson has compared present overcrowding at the state penitentiary to conditions in 1980 that led to the deaths of 33 inmates in a bloody riot.
